headline: 6 Ethereum addresses catalogued (old RUNE token, Router v4.1.1, 2 older routers, deployer EOA, token owner); THORChain native vaults are dynamically rotated TSS Asgard vaults with no fixed EVM address; Router V6.1 deployed but on-chain address not resolved this run.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 4 THORChain-labelled contracts on Ethereum: 'THORCHAIN: Old RUNE Token' (0x3155ba), 'THORChain: THORChain Router v4.1.1' (0xD37BbE), an earlier Router (0x42A5Ed), and 'THORSwap: RouterV2' (0xc14599). Also surfaced deployer EOA 0x3eff38. CertiK scan provided token owner address 0x18f773. No addresses found on other EVM chains (BSC, Avalanche, Base) in this run due to search exhaustion.

D2: No canonical 'Deployed Contracts' / 'Addresses' page found on thorchain.org or dev.thorchain.org during this run. The dev.thorchain.org intro page references an /inbound_addresses API endpoint for fetching the current dynamic Asgard vault address at runtime, rather than a static deployments list. The dev.thorchain.org 'sending transactions' page confirms the Router contract address is used for EVM deposits but does not list a static address. deployed_contracts_doc set to null.

D3: GitHub search snippet (github.com/thorchain/Resources/tree/master/Audits) lists three audit PDFs: Halborn-StateMachine-Router-Bifrost-Audit-Sep2021.pdf, Halborn-TSS-Audit-Sep2021.pdf, THORChain-TrailOfBits-FullAudit-Aug2021.pdf, and THORChain Bifrost - Zellic Audit Report Draft.pdf. Direct fetch of github.com was blocked. CertiK skynet page lists 1 CertiK audit (Oct 2021, scope: gitlab.com/THORChain/thornode) and references 3 third-party audits total. Code4rena 2024 contest (code-423n4/2024-06-thorchain) focused on Router V5 removal of whitelisting — audit-era contract addresses not resolved this run.

D4: GitHub (github.com/thorchain) is confirmed to exist per CertiK page. Primary source repo is GitLab: gitlab.com/thorchain/thornode. github.com domain was blocked for direct fetch. No deployment artifact files (broadcast JSON, hardhat-deploy, deployments.json) could be walked this run. GitLab repo confirmed from dev.thorchain.org and thorchain.org footer.

D5: Protocol spans 13 chains. Only Ethereum EVM addresses were surfaced in this run via Etherscan. For BSC, Avalanche, Base — which also have EVM routers per the dev docs ('Each connected EVM-based ETH forks have a router') — no addresses were resolved due to search exhaustion. THORChain native chain, Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Ripple, Tron, Cosmos, Solana are UTXO/non-EVM chains where funds flow to dynamically-rotated TSS Asgard vault addresses, not fixed contracts. D5: chain BSC: zero EVM router addresses surfaced. D5: chain Avalanche: zero EVM router addresses surfaced. D5: chain Base: zero EVM router addresses surfaced.

D6: No factory contracts identified in this run. THORChain pools are managed natively on the THORChain L1 rather than via EVM factory contracts. The THORChain native pool enumeration API exists at /pools endpoint (e.g. thorchain.net/pools/main referenced on website) but is a Cosmos REST endpoint, not an EVM factory. No D6 on-chain factory reads performed.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: old RUNE token = token; Router v4.1.1 = router; earlier Router = router (deprecated); THORSwap RouterV2 = router (audit-era); deployer EOA = other; token owner = owner. All entries recorded in admin_addresses.

D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to fetched Etherscan or CertiK URLs. Router V6.1 address was mentioned in blog search snippet but the address itself was not found in fetched URL bodies — recorded in unknowns[] per D8 rule.

rationale.verdict: Walked thorchain.org (website), skynet.certik.com (audit/token page), etherscan.io (RUNE token contract), dev.thorchain.org (dev docs), and search results referencing Etherscan name tags. 6 Ethereum addresses catalogued. THORChain's primary control surface on non-EVM chains is dynamically-rotated TSS Asgard vaults with no fixed on-chain addresses; only EVM chains have fixed Router contracts. BSC/Avalanche/Base router addresses not resolved due to tool-call exhaustion.

protocol_metadata.about: THORChain is a decentralised cross-chain liquidity protocol that enables users to swap native assets (BTC, ETH, ATOM, etc.) across 14 blockchains directly from self-custody wallets, without wrapped tokens or bridges. It operates as a Cosmos-based Layer 1 where a permissionless network of ~107 bonded nodes form TSS (Threshold Signature Scheme) Asgard vaults that hold deposited assets. On EVM chains, users interact with a stateless Router smart contract that emits events observed by the Bifrost module, which coordinates swaps through native RUNE-paired liquidity pools.
